why: Paid media is where much of the marketing budget goes and where results are measured to the euro. Performance marketing, traffic manager and social media roles all ask for hands-on Google Ads and Meta experience.
outcome: structure a Google Ads search campaign, pick match types and negative keywords, explain Quality Score and the auction, choose a bidding strategy, set up a Meta campaign, plan organic social content and read a campaign report to move budget.

lessons.title: Paid search: how the auction works
text: Search ads appear when someone types a query that matches your keywords. Each time, Google runs an auction among the eligible ads. The position depends on Ad Rank: your bid, the quality of the ad and landing page, the context of the search and your ad assets (extra links, phone number, location).
You pay per click (CPC), and usually less than your maximum bid: just enough to keep your position. A better ad can therefore win a higher position for a lower price.
points: Paid search captures existing demand: people who already look for a solution.
Ad Rank is not just the bid: quality lets small advertisers compete.
Brand campaigns (your own name) are cheap and protect you from competitors bidding on it.
Ads are labelled 'Sponsored'; organic results are separate.

lessons.title: Structuring a Google Ads campaign
text: An account holds campaigns; a campaign sets the budget, the bidding strategy, the locations and the languages; it holds ad groups, each with a tight set of keywords and the ads written for them.

Keywords use match types: broad match (related searches, the widest), phrase match (the meaning of the phrase, written in quotes) and exact match (the same meaning, in brackets). Negative keywords exclude searches you do not want, such as 'free' or 'jobs'. Responsive search ads combine up to 15 headlines and 4 descriptions and Google tests the combinations.
points: One theme per ad group, so the ad matches the search.
Read the search terms report every week and add negatives.
Broad match works best with smart bidding and good conversion data.
Write headlines that repeat the query, a benefit and a reason to click now.

example.code:
Account: StrideLab
└─ Campaign: Search - Flat feet - FR      (budget 40 EUR/day, bidding: Maximize conversions)
   ├─ Ad group: Running shoes flat feet
   │   ├─ Keywords: "running shoes flat feet"  [best running shoes for flat feet]
   │   ├─ Negative keywords: free, used, diy
   │   └─ Responsive search ad (up to 15 headlines, 4 descriptions)
   └─ Ad group: Arch support insoles
       ├─ Keywords: "arch support insoles"  [insoles for flat feet]
       └─ Responsive search ad
example.note: Phrase match in quotes, exact match in brackets, negatives at the ad group or campaign level.

lessons.title: Quality Score, ads and landing pages
text: Quality Score (1 to 10, per keyword) is a diagnostic built from three parts: expected click-through rate, ad relevance (does the ad match the search?) and landing page experience (does the page deliver what the ad promised, fast, on mobile?).

Improving them lowers cost and raises position. Write ads that use the words of the search, send each ad group to the most specific page, and keep the promise of the ad on the page: same offer, same price, a clear call to action.
points: Quality Score is a guide, not what the auction uses directly.
A generic home page as landing page usually hurts conversion.
Use assets: sitelinks, callouts, structured snippets, call and location.
Test one change at a time (headline, offer, page) and compare conversion rates.

example.code:
Headline 1  : Running Shoes for Flat Feet        (max 30 characters)
Headline 2  : Tested by Podiatrists
Headline 3  : Free 30-Day Returns
Description : Compare 12 shoes with real arch support. Free size guide, delivery in 48 h. (max 90)
Final URL   : https://stridelab.example/flat-feet
Path        : stridelab.example/Running/Flat-Feet
example.note: Headlines 30 characters, descriptions 90: say the query, the proof and the offer.

lessons.title: Bidding, budgets and conversion tracking
text: Smart bidding lets Google set the bid for each auction from many signals. Maximize conversions spends the budget to get as many conversions as possible; Target CPA aims for an average cost per conversion; Target ROAS aims for a revenue-to-cost ratio; Maximize clicks or manual CPC fit when there is no conversion data yet.

Smart bidding is only as good as the conversions it learns from. Track the real goal (purchase, qualified lead), give it a value, avoid counting the same conversion twice, and leave a new strategy a learning period of about two weeks before judging it.
points: Set the target from history: a Target CPA far below reality stops delivery.
Performance Max runs one campaign across Search, YouTube, Display, Gmail, Maps and Discover.
Budget limited campaigns miss auctions: raise the budget or narrow the targeting.
Import offline conversions (signed deals) so bidding learns what really brings money.

lessons.title: Paid social: Meta, LinkedIn and TikTok
text: Social ads create demand: people are not searching, so the creative must stop the scroll. On Meta (Facebook, Instagram), a campaign chooses an objective (awareness, traffic, engagement, leads, app promotion, sales), an ad set chooses the audience, placements, budget and schedule, and the ad holds the creative.

Audiences: broad targeting with good creatives often works best today, plus custom audiences (your customers, site visitors, video viewers) for retargeting and lookalike audiences built from your best customers. LinkedIn targets by job title, company and industry, which suits B2B at a higher cost per click. Measure with the Meta Pixel and the Conversions API (server side).
points: The objective decides who Meta shows the ad to: choose the result you really want.
Vertical video (9:16) for Reels and Stories; the first 3 seconds decide.
Refresh creatives when frequency rises and results fall (ad fatigue).
Exclude existing customers from prospecting campaigns.

example.code:
Campaign  : objective "Sales" (what Meta optimizes for)
└─ Ad set : audience (France, 25-45, interest: running) + placements + budget + schedule
   └─ Ad  : creative (video 9:16 or image 1:1), primary text, headline, call to action, URL with UTM
example.note: The same three levels exist on LinkedIn and TikTok, with different names.

lessons.title: Organic social media
text: Organic social is what a brand posts without paying: it builds community, trust and reach over time, and gives paid campaigns proof and content. Each network has its own format and audience: LinkedIn for professionals and B2B, Instagram and TikTok for visual and short video, Facebook for communities and local, X and Threads for news and conversation.

Work with content pillars (three to five recurring themes), an editorial calendar and a steady rhythm. Measure engagement rate, reach, saves and shares, clicks to the site and the leads or sales they bring; answer comments and messages quickly.
points: Adapt each post to the network: do not copy the same text everywhere.
Employees and creators often reach further than the brand page.
Plan for moderation and a crisis process before you need them.
Social media managers report on business results, not only followers.

lessons.title: Reading a campaign report and moving budget
text: A report compares campaigns on the same metrics: spend, clicks, conversions, cost per acquisition (CPA) and return on ad spend (ROAS). Look for what to scale (low CPA, high ROAS, still budget limited), what to fix (high CPA: search terms, ad, page) and what to stop.

Be careful with attribution: platforms each claim the sale. Brand search and retargeting look excellent because they reach people who were already going to buy; prospecting looks weaker but creates the future demand. Compare platforms with your analytics tool and, when possible, with incrementality tests (holdout groups).
points: Judge a campaign on its role in the funnel, not on ROAS alone.
Look at enough data: a few conversions do not prove anything.
Move budget in steps (around 20 % at a time) to keep learning stable.
Write down each change and its date, to read the results later.

example.code:
Campaign             Spend   Clicks  Conv.  Revenue  CPC    CPA    ROAS
Search - Brand       300     1,200   120    9,600    0.25   2.50   32.0
Search - Flat feet   1,800   2,000   60     6,000    0.90   30.00  3.3
Meta - Prospecting   2,400   6,000   40     3,200    0.40   60.00  1.3
Meta - Retargeting   500     900     35     3,500    0.56   14.29  7.0
example.note: Brand search and retargeting have the best ROAS, but they mostly harvest demand that prospecting created.

items: Bid × quality × context × assets: decides position
Searches with the meaning of the phrase
Excludes searches you do not want
1–10: expected CTR, ad relevance, landing page experience
Average cost per conversion aimed for
Revenue per euro of ad cost aimed for
One campaign on all Google channels
Your customers, visitors or video viewers
People similar to your best customers
Average times a person saw the ad
Compare with a group that saw no ads

pitfalls: Sending every ad to the home page instead of the most relevant page.
Never reading the search terms report, so the budget pays for useless searches.
Optimizing a Meta campaign for clicks when the goal is sales.
Judging a new bidding strategy after two days, during its learning period.
Cutting prospecting because brand search and retargeting show a better ROAS.

exercises.q: A campaign spent 1,800 € and brought 6,000 € of revenue. What is its ROAS?
exercises.answer: ROAS = revenue / spend = 6,000 / 1,800 ≈ 3.3: each euro of advertising brought about 3.33 € of revenue (before costs and margin).

exercises.q: Match each keyword with its match type.
exercises.answer: No sign is broad match, quotes are phrase match, brackets are exact match, and a minus sign marks a negative keyword in the editor.

exercises.q: Which three parts make up the Google Ads Quality Score?
options: Expected CTR, ad relevance, landing page experience
Number of keywords, ad length, account age
exercises.answer: Quality Score combines expected click-through rate, ad relevance and landing page experience. The bid is part of Ad Rank, not of Quality Score.

exercises.q: Sort these into paid search and paid social.
exercises.answer: Paid search answers a query that someone typed; paid social places a creative in a feed in front of an audience you chose.

exercises.q: Your Meta prospecting campaign has a ROAS of 1.3 and retargeting a ROAS of 7. Your manager wants to stop prospecting. What do you do?

choices.label: Explain that retargeting needs new visitors that prospecting brings
choices.feedback: Retargeting audiences shrink without prospecting; its ROAS is partly borrowed from it.

choices.label: Stop prospecting and put everything into retargeting
choices.feedback: The retargeting audience runs out within weeks and its results fall too.

steps.text: How do you prove the value of prospecting?

choices.label: Run a holdout test: a region or audience without prospecting for a few weeks
choices.feedback: An incrementality test measures what the ads really add, beyond what each platform claims.

exercises.answer: Judge each campaign on its role in the funnel. Retargeting harvests demand that prospecting creates; prove it with an incrementality (holdout) test before cutting.

exercises.q: Put the steps of a Google Ads weekly check in a sensible order.
steps: Check that conversions are being recorded
Read the search terms report and add negative keywords
Compare CPA and ROAS by campaign
Move budget towards the campaigns that perform
Write down the changes and their date
exercises.answer: First make sure tracking works (otherwise every number is wrong), then clean the traffic, then compare, then act, then log what you changed.

exercises.q: A yoga studio in Lyon has 600 € a month for ads. Propose a split between Google and Meta and say what you would measure.
exercises.answer: Example: about 60 % Google Search (studio name, “yoga Lyon”, “cours de yoga débutant Lyon”, location assets, a first-class-free page) because people already search; about 40 % Meta (Instagram Reels of real classes, people within 5 km, 25–55, retargeting of site visitors and video viewers). Measure trial bookings per channel (UTM and conversion tracking), cost per booking, and how many trials become paying members after a month.

interview.q: What decides the position of an ad on Google?
interview.a: Ad Rank: the bid, the quality of the ad and landing page (expected CTR, relevance, page experience), the context of the search and the ad assets. A better ad can rank higher and pay less per click.

interview.q: When would you use Target ROAS instead of Target CPA?
interview.a: When conversions have different values, like e-commerce orders, and the goal is revenue relative to cost. Target CPA fits when each conversion is worth about the same, like lead forms.

interview.q: How do you lower a high cost per acquisition on Google Ads?
interview.a: Check tracking first, then the search terms for irrelevant traffic (negatives, match types), the ad and landing page relevance, the bids and targets by device and location, and the offer itself. One change at a time, measured over enough conversions.

interview.q: How do you structure a Meta campaign for an e-commerce brand?
interview.a: A sales-objective prospecting campaign with broad audiences or lookalikes and several creatives, a retargeting campaign for visitors and cart abandoners with product ads, existing customers excluded from prospecting, and Pixel plus Conversions API for tracking.

interview.q: Platforms each claim the same sale. How do you report?
interview.a: I use one neutral source, the analytics tool or the CRM, with a stated attribution model, show platform figures as a second view, and use incrementality tests for the big budget decisions.

interview.q: How do you measure organic social media?
interview.a: Reach and engagement rate per post and per pillar, saves and shares, clicks to the site with UTM links, and the leads or sales they bring; followers alone are not a result.
